question: Using suitable determinant operations, show that $$\begin{vmatrix}1+a&1&1\\1&1+b&1\\1&1&1+c\end{vmatrix}=ab+bc+ca+abc.$$
explanation:
Row simplification
Apply $R_2\to R_2-R_1$ and $R_3\to R_3-R_1$. The determinant becomes $$\begin{vmatrix}1+a&1&1\\-a&b&0\\-a&0&c\end{vmatrix}$$
Expansion along the first row
Expanding the transformed determinant, $$D=(1+a)bc-1\begin{vmatrix}-a&0\\-a&c\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}-a&b\\-a&0\end{vmatrix}$$
Evaluation of the minors
Therefore, $$D=bc(1+a)-(-ac)+ab$$
Algebraic simplification
Thus, $$D=bc+abc+ac+ab=ab+bc+ca+abc$$
Hence, the required result is established.
